cultural.vision_reason: The image shows a woman's tube skirt (phasin) with horizontal polychrome banding in red, blue, orange and dark indigo sections, a textile style consistent with hill-tribe weaving traditions of the Lahu in Myanmar. The garment type and construction match plausible Lahu dress even though pattern alone cannot rule out neighbouring groups.

physical.title: skirt
physical.summary: A woman's tube skirt, a phasin.  Made of three unequal sized pieces of tabby cotton cloth (paired warps) with polychrome bands (woven as stripes).  Top section [32 cms deep] has cream band (single warps), with evenly spaced polychrome bands on a red 'ground' below; red weft.  Middle section [27.5 cms] has red band with three fine blue bands (upper), with thin polychrome bands below; red weft.  Lowest section [30 cms] is make of dark blue cloth, broken up with five groups of fine applied red bands and lines of white, pale blue or orange stitching at one edge; blue weft.  All joins hand stitched.
